caption:
Eighty percent of India's C-suite is cutting management layers. Globally that number is 59%. India is flattening faster than anyone.

Here is what that actually means for you. The manager who used to carry your work upstairs — who said your name in rooms you weren't in — that role is being deleted. Nobody is translating your contribution anymore.

So the impression forms directly. Fewer encounters. Higher stakes. One meeting with a senior leader now does the work that six months of a manager's advocacy used to do.

In command, you learn this early: when the chain shortens, bearing carries what reporting used to. How you enter. How you hold a pause before you answer. Whether your voice drops or climbs when you're challenged.

The layer above you was insulation. It was also a filter. It is going away.

Be legible without it.

topic.title: The Great Flattening: 80% of India's C-suite cutting layers
topic.angle: This audience sits in or just below the management layer being deleted — with no manager to translate their contribution upward, senior impressions now form directly in fewer, higher-stakes encounters.
topic.why_now: The India-specific 80% figure (vs 59% globally) is about a month old but fresh commentary landed two days ago, and it pairs directly with the September Microsoft agentic-AI data as a two-parter.

rationale: A stark two-number typographic slide lets the India-vs-global gap land instantly and matches the brand's plainspoken, no-decoration authority.
